verdict.rationale: Reflect's documented OAuth2 REST API lets an agent write headlessly: it can create notes and append to daily notes. However, the vendor states plainly that note contents are end-to-end encrypted and cannot be served through the API, so agents cannot read notes. Read access is limited to graphs, bookmarked links and the user profile. missing for 10: API read access to note contents, an MCP server or local API, full note editing/update endpoints, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent or assistant can read AND write my notes headlessly — through a documented local API, vendor API, or MCP server — without me touching the GUI

citations.quote: PUT /graphs/{graphId}/daily-notes, POST /graphs/{graphId}/notes, and GET /users/me with OAuth2 scopes read:graph / write:graph
Your notes contents are end-to-end encrypted. Our servers can't read the contents of your notes, so we can't serve them up in the API.
Our supports appending data to your notes, returning a list of the links you've bookmarked, and a few other things.
